cf.title: [BUG] Fix EXCLUDED virtual generated columns using tableoid

input.subject: [BUG] ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET x = EXCLUDED.<virtual-generated-column> errors or silently writes NULL

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal or the choice to raise an error: v2 follows Dean Rasheed's argument that EXCLUDED has no system columns. Two fixable design points remain. standards-compat-1 asks whether a back-patch to v18 may make statements fail that run today. standards-compat-2 asks whether stored and virtual columns over tableoid now behave differently in EXCLUDED. Both are release and consistency decisions for a committer who knows this area.

brief.title: Reject tableoid in EXCLUDED virtual generated column expansion
brief.problem: Commit 783425175 (back-patched to v18) stopped expanding virtual generated columns in the EXCLUDED target list. Since then, a virtual column whose expression uses tableoid, referenced as excluded.c in ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, fails with the internal error "variable not found in subplan target lists". In some WHERE cases a reviewer saw it run without error instead.
brief.proposed_design: v1 added a tableoid entry to the EXCLUDED target list so the reference resolves. After Dean Rasheed objected that EXCLUDED is a proposed row with no system columns, v2 rejects the expanded tableoid reference with a user-facing error. The check sits in expand_virtual_generated_columns() in prepjointree.c, with a regression test.
user_visible_surface: New error: cannot use system column "tableoid" in EXCLUDED, raised when excluded.<virtual column> expands to an expression using tableoid.
Statements that ran before, such as WHERE excluded.c IS NOT NULL with a tableoid-based column, now fail with this error.
author_claims: v2 turns the internal "variable not found in subplan target lists" error into a proper error for the reported case.
The author is unsure whether to back-patch to PG 18.
brief.thread_state: Dean Rasheed argued for an error and Ayush posted v2 to match. João Rito tested v2 on master and confirmed it works, and suggested naming the column in the message; placement, message wording and back-patching are still open.
unclear: The CF entry title says "Fix" and targets stable, but v2 is a rejection; the material does not say whether the v18 back-patch will happen.
v2 does not say whether other system columns (ctid, xmin) in a generation expression need the same check.
v2 does not say why some unpatched WHERE cases ran without error, or which tableoid value they used.
The material shows prose for the first patch only; the v2 commit message is not shown.

prior_attempts.title: COPY WHERE clause generated/system column reference
prior_attempts.quote: This seems fundamentally wrong, because generated columns are a property of the target table, but the COPY WHERE clause is meant to filter the input data.
prior_attempts.reason: Peter Eisentraut committed a smaller fix that rejects generated columns in COPY FROM WHERE with a clear error, and left tableoid for a separate thread. He then argued that support should not be added, because generated columns belong to the target table while the WHERE clause filters input data. Masahiko Sawada had shown that computing stored generated columns before the WHERE clause runs them before BEFORE INSERT triggers, so the WHERE clause changes the row the trigger sees.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 tried to make generated columns work in COPY FROM WHERE, which filters input rows. v2 here does what that thread chose: it rejects the reference with a clear error instead of giving the proposed row a value.

objections.title: Back-patching a new error breaks statements that run today on v18
objections.failure_scenario: An application on 18.x runs INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE excluded.c IS NOT NULL, where c is a virtual column over tableoid. Message #11 shows this succeeds and updates rows on the unpatched build. After a minor update with v2, the same statement fails with the new error, and the application stops writing at upgrade time.
objections.argument: Message #11 shows WHERE cases that run without error before v2 and fail after it, on plain and partitioned tables. The CF entry targets stable, and message #10 leaves the back-patch open. Turning an internal error into a user-facing error is safe to back-patch, but these cases do not raise an internal error today. The proposal does not say why they work or what tableoid value they see, so nobody can judge whether their results are wrong enough to justify failing them in a minor release.
objections.author_must_show: Do the WHERE cases that succeed today give wrong results, and if not, why should a minor release make them fail?

critic.reasoning: Message #11 shows WHERE excluded.c IS NOT NULL runs on the unpatched build and fails with v2. Message #10 leaves the back-patch open, and the thread does not explain why those cases run today.

objections.title: Stored and virtual columns over tableoid may differ in EXCLUDED
objections.failure_scenario: A user defines c as GENERATED ALWAYS AS (tableoid) STORED and uses excluded.c in ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE. They then change c to VIRTUAL. If the stored form likely yields the target partition's oid, the same statement now fails with the new error, and the user finds out only when it runs.
objections.argument: Dean's case in message #9 compares the rule with a direct reference to excluded.tableoid, which is a reasonable comparison. It does not cover a stored column over tableoid, whose value is computed for the proposed row before the conflict check. Message #11 tested a stored column over b * 10 only. If the stored form works, v2 adds a new difference between virtual and stored columns, and the documentation would need to describe it.
objections.author_must_show: What does excluded.c return for a stored generated column over tableoid, and is the virtual-only error documented as an intended difference?

critic.reasoning: Postgres allows tableoid in a stored generation expression, and the thread does not compare that case with the new virtual-only error. The stored-to-virtual scenario is weak because it needs a drop and re-add of the column, but the consistency question is unanswered.

committability.owner_note: Peter Eisentraut is the assigned committer on the CF entry, and Dean Rasheed set the direction in the thread. The owner needs to know virtual generated column expansion and ON CONFLICT planning.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a new user-facing error in ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE and, if back-patched, for statements that stop working in a v18 minor release. The check is small and adds no persistent state.

priority.reason: Few users define a virtual generated column over tableoid and reference it through EXCLUDED, but the current result is an internal error in v18. The check is small, a committer is assigned, and the open points are the back-patch decision and the stored-column comparison.

precedents_retrieved.title: generated columns
precedents_retrieved.summary: Peter Eisentraut proposed implementing SQL-standard generated columns (GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expr)), with the generation expression stored in pg_attrdef like a default and MySQL/Oracle-style VIRTUAL|STORED syntax. Only the VIRTUAL (computed-on-read) variant was fully implemented; STORED, various ALTER TABLE forms and index support were deferred.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Review by Jaime Casanova found multiple bugs: generated columns showed no value through a view, inheritance produced a malformed default and a server crash on insert, ALTER COLUMN TYPE on the referenced or generated column failed with internal errors, triggers saw NULL for the generated column, and the generation expression could be dropped via DROP DEFAULT. Based on these reviews, the commitfest manager marked the entry Returned with feedback, asking for an updated version to be resubmitted.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reduce the log spam by excluding certain SQLSTATEs
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a setting, log_suppress_errcodes, that stops ERROR and FATAL messages with the listed SQLSTATEs from reaching the server log. Early versions shipped a non-empty default list of common codes such as 23505 and 42P01, and later versions default to an empty list and skip logical replication workers.
precedents_retrieved.objection: After the patch was marked ready for committer, Fujii Masao argued that filtering by SQLSTATE alone does not belong in core. Users may also want to filter by application name, client host, database or role, and core cannot support all of these, so an extension using emit_log_hook fits better. Tom Lane agreed that the filtering is too opinionated for elog.c and would suit a contrib module, and the author withdrew the patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: Exclude partition constaint checking in query execution plan for partitioned table queries
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the planner remove restriction clauses from scans of partitions or inheritance children when those clauses are already implied by the partition or CHECK constraints, to avoid redundant filter evaluation. Earlier versions also extended operator_predicate_proof (first with hard-coded integer operators, later with a range-type lookup) so that, for example, k < 20001 could prove k <= 20000.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was returned with feedback because the latest reviews had not been addressed. David Rowley rejected the range-type approach to predicate proof, for performance, collation and pg_range scan reasons, and asked that the predicate_implied_by() changes become a separate patch. He also asked for new benchmarks on planning overhead. His last review raised a concern that removing quals could prevent an index such as (a,b) from being used. Andres Freund raised an earlier concern about planning overhead, but his message is not shown.

This reverts commit 083d29c65b7897f90c70e6dc0a4240a5fa75c8f2.

The commit changed the code so that it causes an errors when

precedents_retrieved.title: Rearrange execution of PARAM_EXTERN Params for plpgsql's benefit.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Rearrange execution of PARAM_EXTERN Params for plpgsql's benefit.
Reverted commit(s): Further reduce overhead for passing plpgsql variables to the executor.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This patch does three interrelated things:

* Create a new expression execution step type EEOP_PARAM_CALLBACK
and add the infrastructure needed for add-on modules to generate that.
As discussed, the best control mechanism for that seems to be to add
another hook function to ParamListInfo, which will be called by
ExecInitExpr if it's supplied and a PARAM_EXTERN Param is found.
For stand-alone expressions, we add a new entry point to allow the
ParamListInfo to be specified directly, since it can't be retrieved
from the parent plan node's EState.

* Redesign the API for the ParamListInfo paramFetch hook so that the
ParamExternData array can be entirely virtual.  This also lets us get rid
of ParamListInfo.paramMask, instead leaving it to the paramFetch hook to
decide which param IDs should be accessible or not.  plpgsql_param_fetch
was already doing the identical masking check, so having callers do it too
seemed redundant.  While I was at it, I added a "speculative" flag to
paramFetch that the planner can specify as TRUE to avoid unwanted failures.
This solves an ancient problem for plpgsql that it couldn't provide values
of non-DTYPE_VAR variables to the planner for fear of triggering premature
"record not assigned yet" or "field not found" errors during planning.

* Rework plpgsql to get rid of the need for "unshared" parameter lists,
by dint of turning the single ParamListInfo per estate into a nearly
read-only data structure that doesn't instantiate any per-variable data.
Instead, the paramFetch hook controls access to per-variable data and can
make the right decisions on the fly, replacing the cases that we used to
need multiple ParamListInfos for.  This might perhaps have been a
performance loss on its own, but by using a paramCompile hook we can
bypass plpgsql_param_fetch entirely during normal query execution.
(It's now only called when, eg, we copy the ParamListInfo into a cursor
portal.  copyParamList() or SerializeParamList() effectively instantiate
the virtual parameter array as a simple physical array without a
paramFetch hook, which is what we want in those cases.)  This allows
reverting most of commit 6c82d8d1f, though I kept the cosmetic
code-consolidation aspects of that (eg the assign_simple_var function).

Performance testing shows this to be at worst a break-even change,
and it can provide wins ranging up to 20% in test cases involving
accesses to fields of "record" variables.  The fact that values of
such variables can now be exposed to the planner might produce wins
in some situations, too, but I've not pursued that angle.

In passing, remove the "parent" pointer from the arguments to
ExecInitExprRec and related functions, instead storing that pointer in a
transient field in ExprState.  The ParamListInfo pointer for a stand-alone
expression is handled the same way; we'd otherwise have had to add
yet another recursively-passed-down argument in expression compilation.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow self-conflicting INSERT INTO .. ON CONFLICT DO UPDATEs
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE accept a command whose own proposed rows conflict with each other, as DO NOTHING already does. Today such a command fails with "command cannot affect row a second time".
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund and Peter Geoghegan voted against it, and the CFM returned it citing those two votes. Andres Freund objected that the patch makes one command update a row it inserted, producing cmin == cmax and breaking heap visibility rules. The author then found visibility bugs in his own patch. Peter Geoghegan argued that updating the same row twice in one command is not desirable and asked who would want it.

precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Allow ON CONFLICT .. DO NOTHING on a partitioned table."
Reverted commit(s): Allow ON CONFLICT .. DO NOTHING on a partitioned table.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 8355a011a0124bdf7ccbada206a967d427039553, which
turns out to have been a misguided effort.  We can't really support
this in a partitioning hierarchy after all for exactly the reasons
stated in the documentation removed by that commit.  It's still
possible to use ON CONFLICT .. DO NOTHING (or for that matter ON
CONFLICT .. DO UPDATE) on individual partitions if desired, but
but to allow this on a partitioned table implies that we have some
way of evaluating uniqueness across the whole partitioning
hierarchy, which is false.

Shinoda Noriyoshi noticed that the old code was crashing (which we
could fix, though not in a nice way) and Amit Langote realized
that this was indicative of a fundamental problem with the commit
being reverted here.

roaster_notes.note: The only related precedent, P1, rejected giving input-side rows target-table values. v2 follows that reasoning, as Dean Rasheed argued in messages #7 and #9, so no earlier rejection reason applies against it. The earlier fix in this thread (message #4, commit 783425175) caused this regression and was not rejected.
Other system columns are not a gap, because generation expressions already reject system columns other than tableoid. The message wording point in message #11 is minor and left to review.

v2 adds a parse-time check in expand_virtual_generated_columns() and nothing persistent or cross-node: no on-disk, WAL, catalog, protocol or ABI change. Virtual columns are not stored, so old or upgraded data is unaffected; whether to back-patch to v18 is a compatibility question for another angle.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. v2 replaces an internal error with a user-facing error when excluded.<virtual column> expands to tableoid; it grants no new access, reveals no data, and adds no denial-of-service path. The error names only a column of a table the user already has privileges to insert into.

From the maintenance and fit angle there is nothing to object to. The change is a small check that runs only while virtual generated columns are being expanded, and it adds no GUC, catalog or API. Dean Rasheed knows the area and set the direction in message #7 and message #9, and Peter Eisentraut is the assigned committer, so ownership is clear. Generation expressions already reject system columns other than tableoid, so a tableoid-only check covers every case. [P1] concerns a different feature, COPY FROM WHERE, and does not apply here. The open questions are about release handling, not long-run maintenance: whether a new error belongs in a back-patch to 18, and why some unpatched WHERE cases ran without error.

The proposal fixes a planner internal error in core ON CONFLICT handling. No existing feature, setting or extension can avoid the error or reject the case properly, so the need is not already met. The one existing behaviour, the parser error for direct excluded.tableoid, is what v2 follows; message wording is out of scope here.

This is a bug fix: since commit 783425175 the reported statement fails with an internal error, so demand evidence is not needed. Back-patching and the WHERE cases that ran before the patch and now fail are back-patch and design questions, outside the demand angle.
